To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inflammation can contribute to tumours in different ways, and that tumour growth is a dynamic process that involves a complex interplay between the tumour, the host and the environment in which tumours grow.
the quality and quantity of the inflammatory response and the time point of the response may determine whether inflammation is tumour promoting or tumour suppressing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inflammation in cancer development and cancer therapy.
the question of how the immune system can be used to induce tumour rejection.
the identification of tumour growth-promoting and tumour growth-inhibiting inflammatory responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inflammation may support tumour growth, but may also contribute to tumour suppression and that this depends on the nature and quality of the inflammatory response and on its time of appearance in the tumour microenvironment.
inflammation may be beneficial or detrimental for tumour growth and that the role of inflammation is dependent on the quality, quantity and the time point of the response.
inflammation can support tumour growth and can contribute to tumours suppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality, quantity and timing of the inflammatory response determine whether inflammation supports or suppresses tumour growth.
inflammation may support or inhibit tumour growth and that the quality, quantity and timing of the inflammatory response are critical for the tumour outcome.
tumours are not simply a mass of malignant cells but rather a complex structure of malignant and non-malignant cells that have to be understood in their mutual interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of inflammation in cancer is complex.
the inflammatory response is a complex phenomenon and that its outcome depends on the quality and quantity of the response and on the time point at which it occurs.
the quality and timing of the inflammatory response are critical determinants of the outcome of the tumour-host interaction.
